comments.body:
No need for panic.

I got a 2.2 in my undergraduate as I also suffered very badly from depression during my studies for several years.

I went on to get my masters and PhD with no problems. What matters more is your actual intelligence, and at a certain point it becomes obvious to professors. I’m currently doing a postdoc in a very prestigious group (in my field), and what’s more is I was invited to the position based on my publishing record, it had nothing to do with my grades. I’m applying for grants now for my own group.

I do understand where you’re coming from though, I had terrible anxiety about my grades for years (which were actually not good, nothing like yours!) and I thought I had ruined my life and that there was no point in living anymore as I was such a failure. I’m glad I got the help for my mental health that I really needed, because all those bad thoughts were not actually reflective of reality.

Don’t worry, you’re going to be fine.
comments.author: radfemagogo
